newsitem.title: USA: Recording industry amends lawsuit against Amway. [CORRECTED 00:20 GMT 27/11]
newsitem.headline: Recording industry amends lawsuit against Amway. [CORRECTED 00:20 GMT 27/11]

text.p: Twelve major record labels Monday amended a lawsuit against Amway and some of its distributors accusing them of unauthorized use of copyrighted material by Michael Jackson, the Beatles and other artists, raising the damages sought to $19 million from $11 million.

"Since the filing of the initial complaint in February 1996, our efforts have provided considerable additional evidence on infringing activities -- far beyound that known or suspected at the time of the initial civil action," said Hilary Rosen, president of the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), a trade group representing the recording industry.

In the initial complaint, the association, acting on behalf of 11 companies, had sought $11 million in damages against Amway and about 40 distributors for using music in motivational videos at conventions without obtaining clearance from the musicians or their labels.
"We have added 114 new counts of infringements to the original 125, the number of defendants has increased from 40 to 86, and there is one additional record company plaintiff," Rosen said.
The RIAA said the National Music Publishers Association was also expected to file a similar action based on the same videotapes.

Amway, a multibillion-dollar Ada, Mich.-based seller of nutritional items and household products to individual distributors, said it will continue to vigorously defend itself against the allegations made by both associations. It said it would also continue working with representatives of both groups to investigate and resolve the charges.

"Amway Corp. is disappointed by the RIAA's decision to escalate this litigation and particularly by RIAA's continuing use of the news media to misrepresent the conduct of the parties and the extent of any damages to the record companies," the company said in a statement.

Amway's distributors work on commission and can earn bonuses on sales made by new distributors they recruit. (Corrects to clarify that distributor earnings are based on sales by newly recruited individuals).

The association said the original lawsuit, filed in Orlando, Fla., centers on the production and sale of motivational and promotional videotapes by Amway distributors using hit sound recordings to promote upcoming conventions, recruit additinal Amway distributors and sell Amway products.
It said the National Music Publishers Association was expected to file a similar action based on the same infringing videotapes.

Among the labels filing the suit are Sony Corp.'s Sony Music, Philips Electronics NV's Polygram Records and Motown Records Co., Bertelsmann AG's Arista Records Inc. and BMG Music, Seagram Co. Ltd.'s MCA Records Inc. and several others.
